temaNombre: Text types: stories, poems and news reports
title: Discovering stories, poems and news reports
summary: Learn to tell Spanish stories, poems and news reports apart with fun activities.
keyIdeas: A story tells an imaginary tale with characters.
Many poems are written in lines and may rhyme.
A news report gives information about events that must be checked. The examples in this activity are made up.

activities.prompt: Which Spanish sentence has the form of a news headline? These examples are made up.
activities.explanation: This sentence reports an opening, giving a place and time. A published news report must check that the event happened.
activities.hint: Find the sentence reporting an opening.
options: La luna sonríe vestida de seda blanca.
Ayer abrió la nueva biblioteca del barrio.
Un dragón vuela sobre el castillo encantado.

activities.prompt: Poems often have words that rhyme.
activities.explanation: Many poems play with sounds and rhythm by using rhyme.

activities.prompt: Complete the Spanish sentence with the correct text type.
activities.explanation: News reports tell us about real, recent events in a place.
activities.sentence: Para saber qué pasó ayer en mi ciudad leo una ___.

activities.prompt: Match each Spanish opening to its text type.
activities.explanation: «Érase una vez» begins a story, the verse forms part of a poem, and the museum sentence has the form of a news report.

pairs.left: Érase una vez en un bosque lejano...
Verde que te quiero verde, verde viento...
El museo de la ciudad abre mañana sus puertas.

activities.prompt: Sort these made-up Spanish examples by their form: story, poem or news report.
activities.explanation: The examples include fantasy, rhyming lines and informative sentences in the form of news reports.

items.text: La princesa hablaba con un unicornio mágico.
El gato chiquito duerme en su saquito.
Los bomberos rescatan a un perro en el parque.
Había una vez un duende juguetón.
Estrellita de la noche, brillas en mi coche.
El colegio estrena un patio con huerto.

activities.prompt: Read this made-up Spanish example in the form of a news report and answer the questions.
activities.explanation: This example has the form of a news report, but it was made up for practice.
activities.title: Adopción de mascotas
activities.text: El refugio de animales del pueblo celebra hoy una fiesta. Muchas familias han acudido para adoptar perros y gatos sin hogar. Los organizadores afirman que ya han encontrado casa para diez cachorros.

questions.prompt: What type of text is this example?
questions.explanation: It has the form of a news report: it describes an event with a place, time and details.
The text says they have found homes for ten puppies.

activities.prompt: Put the usual parts of a story in order.
activities.explanation: A story begins with an introduction, continues with a problem and ends with a resolution.

activities.prompt: Aisha wants to write a Spanish poem about the sun. Which line uses rhyme?
activities.explanation: «brillante» and «gigante» rhyme because their endings sound alike. This gives the poem rhythm.
activities.hint: Look for words whose endings sound alike.
options: El sol brillante calienta al gigante.
El sol está en el cielo azul.
El sol sale a las siete de la mañana.

activities.prompt: Find the mistake: which Spanish example has the wrong text type?
activities.explanation: Little Red Riding Hood is a traditional fictional story, rather than a newspaper report.
activities.hint: Little Red Riding Hood is a well-known fictional character.
options: «Caperucita roja visitó a su abuela»: News report
«El rey construyó una torre mágica»: Story

activities.prompt: Hugo wants to tell the whole school about a charity match. What should he write?
activities.explanation: An informative notice or news report is suitable for giving information about a real event.
activities.hint: Hugo needs to give real information about when and where the match will be.
options: An informative notice with the match's date and location.
A story about fairies and fast elves.
